_comment: This file holds what JJ Flexible says and shows, for connect and session lifecycle - discovery, SmartLink, connecting, disconnecting, radio selection and diagnostics. EDITING: change the text on the right of the colon; never change the key on the left, and never change anything inside curly braces such as {radio} - those are filled in at run time with the actual radio name, frequency and so on. If an argument goes missing the placeholder is left standing rather than blanked, so you would hear the word radio in braces spoken aloud - that is a bug worth reporting, not something you caused. A key with no text is spoken as the key itself, so if you hear something like connect.radio_found read out literally, that key needs text. LADDERS: a few keys hold several tiers instead of one string - critical, terse, chatty and sometimes diagnostic - which is how one message gets shorter as you turn verbosity down. Edit the tier you want; leave the others alone. YOUR OWN COPY: put a file of this same name in the lexicon folder beside your settings and it layers on top of this one, key by key - you only need the keys you want to change, and everything else keeps working. If your file has a typo in it, it is ignored and this one is used, so a mistake can never stop the program. SOME WORDS ARE ALSO INSTRUCTIONS: a handful of these strings are matched by the program to decide what to do next, so editing them can change behaviour rather than only wording. Those are being untangled; until they are, if something stops working after an edit, that is why. See docs/planning/active/string-store-contract.md.

connect.smartlink.not_registered_body:
This radio is not registered to {account}, the SmartLink account you are signed in with. Registering a radio lets that account reach it over the internet when you are away from your shack. Flex requires you to be physically at the radio with a hand microphone or a CW key plugged in, to prove someone is really there.

{otherAccountsNote}Select the Open Radio Setup button below to open the setup path — registration is step 2. It all happens right here in JJ Flexible Radio Access; SmartSDR is not required.
connect.smartlink.other_accounts_note: One thing to check first: only the signed-in account was asked. If you registered this radio under one of your other saved accounts, switch to that account instead of registering it again — the Manage Accounts button below opens the list.

connect.smartlink.reach_from_away_body:
You are connected to this radio over your own network, and it is not registered with SmartLink under {account}. That is worth one question, and then this will stop asking.

Registering a radio with SmartLink is how you reach it over the internet from somewhere else — a hotel, a friend's shack, the car. If you only ever operate this radio from where you are right now, you do not need it, and nothing about your local operating changes either way.

If you do want it later, Flex requires you to be at the radio with a hand microphone or a CW key plugged in, to prove someone is really there. It all happens right here in JJ Flexible Radio Access; SmartSDR is not required.

{otherAccountsNote}Choose I Only Use This Radio Here and the question is settled for this radio. Choose Open Radio Setup to register it now. Close leaves it open and you will be asked again on a future run.
connect.smartlink.setup_body:
SmartLink is not set up in JJ Flexible Radio Access yet. SmartLink is a service hosted by FlexRadio Systems that lets you connect to and operate this radio over the internet when you are away from your shack. Getting going takes two easy steps. First, you will create a SmartLink account — the account you will use to log into your radio and other Flex services. Second, you will register this newfangled radio of yours so Flex knows it is really yours.

To start, open the Radio menu and choose Manage SmartLink Accounts. Choose Create Account to make your SmartLink account, or New Login if you already have one — either way it all happens right here in JJ Flex, no web page involved. Once you are signed in, step 2 of Radio Setup registers the radio. Note that you must be at (or near) the radio with a hand microphone or a CW key plugged in, to prove you are really there — sorry, Flex's rules, not ours.

The Open Radio Setup button below takes you to the setup path — follow the bouncing ball. SmartSDR is not required for any of it; you can stay in an accessible interface for the whole process. Have fun and good luck!
